## Commonly Asked Questions
Which plan is right for me?
Free is for trying Railway and running a small app at no cost. Hobby is for indie hackers and developers to build and deploy personal projects. Pro is for professional developers and their teams shipping to production. Enterprise is for dev teams building and deploying production applications with large replica size, SLA, and/or compliance needs.
What does the Free plan include?
The Free plan costs $0 per month and includes $1 of usage credits every month, with no credit card required. Services sleep after a few minutes without outbound traffic and wake on the next request. You get 1 project with up to 3 services, up to 1 vCPU and 0.5 GB of RAM per service, 0.5 GB of volume storage, and one-click Postgres, Redis, MySQL and MongoDB. The Free plan does not expire.
Do services on the Free plan sleep or spin down?
Yes. Free plan services are serverless: after 5 to 10 minutes without outbound traffic they sleep, and the next request wakes them. Sleep is based on outbound traffic, so a bot holding a WebSocket or a worker polling a queue keeps itself awake. Hobby and above run always-on.
How does the trial work?
Every new account starts with a 30-day trial that includes a one-time grant of $5 in credits, with no credit card required. The credits apply to any usage on the platform. When the trial ends or the credits run out, running deployments are stopped. You can then downgrade to the Free plan from the Plans page and redeploy within its limits, or upgrade to Hobby or Pro. If you upgrade while you still have trial credits, the remaining balance carries over to your new plan.
How does the Hobby plan included usage work?
Your Hobby plan subscription includes $5 of usage per month. If your total usage at the end of your billing period is $5 or less, you will not be charged extra for usage. If your total usage exceeds $5 in any given billing period, you will be charged total usage.
Does included usage on Hobby accumulate?
Included usage is reset at the end of every billing cycle and does not accumulate over time.
How are sandboxes billed?
Sandboxes run on Railway's VM primitive and bill on VM rates: $50 per GB of memory per month and $50 per vCPU per month, metered per second, plus $0.05 per GB of egress. You pay for the CPU a sandbox actually uses and the memory it holds while running, not for wall-clock uptime, so a sandbox waiting on a model or a user costs almost nothing. Destroyed sandboxes cost nothing, and an idle timeout destroys forgotten ones automatically. Sandbox usage draws from the same included credit as the rest of your plan.
How can I get a receipt?
When you make a payment, you will receive an email with your invoice and receipt attached. You can also find your billing history in Account > Billing.
How to add company details on my invoice?
Head to Account > Billing and click 'Manage Subscription'. From there, you can update your billing information, including billing address and Tax ID.
What payment methods are accepted?
Railway accepts credit cards for plan subscriptions and usage. We support invoice payments for customers on the Enterprise plan.
Can I try Railway without a credit card?
Yes. Neither the trial nor the Free plan requires a credit card. You only need to add a card to upgrade to Hobby or Pro.
Can I upgrade or downgrade at any time?
You can upgrade any time, and when you do, you will get to the features of your new plan, as well as access to more powerful resources, immediately. When you downgrade, the changes will take effect at the beginning of your next billing cycle.
What happens when I cancel my subscription?
When you cancel your subscription, if you're on Hobby or Pro, your plan will remain active through the end of your current billing period, and any usage will be charged at the end of the period. If you are on the Hobby plan and using prepaid credits as your payment method, your subscription will be canceled immediately and any credit balance you may have will be forfeited.
For more information, check out the docs. .
